Kelly Kremer.b:
Kelly Kremer enters his 29th overall season on the University of Minnesota swimming and diving staff and his 15th year leading both programs as Director of Swimming and Diving heading into the 2026–27 season. Under a contract extension securing his leadership through 2028, Kremer continues to guide the Golden Gophers as one of the most consistent and respected leaders in collegiate swimming and diving.
Under Kremer's guidance, Minnesota has maintained a firm standing as a national powerhouse. The Gopher men’s program holds one of the longest streaks in NCAA Division I history, having secured top-25 finishes at the NCAA Championships for 33 consecutive seasons (1992-2024), while the women’s team holds a top-25 streak spanning nearly two decades. Kremer has coached four individual NCAA champions—including Jillian Tyler (2011; 100 breaststroke), Haley Spencer (2011; 200 breaststroke), Kierra Smith (2015; 200 breaststroke), and Max Mchugh (2021; 100 and 200 breaststroke, 2022; 100 breaststroke, 2023; 100 breaststroke)—and established Minnesota’s dominance in the Big Ten with more than 14 individual conference titles in breaststroke events since 2008.
Kremer’s influence extends prominently to the international stage, having coached seven Gopher swimmers to the Olympic Games. Most recently, he coached Bowe Becker to an Olympic Gold Medal with Team USA in the men’s 4x100m freestyle relay at the Tokyo Olympics, making Becker the seventh Gopher in history to earn Olympic gold. His international coaching resume also includes serving as an assistant coach for USA Men at the 2013 World University Games and 2011 Pan American Games, as well as Head Coach for Team Mexico at the 2002 Short Course World Championships. Beyond Becker, Kremer has guided international Olympians James Freeman (Botswana), Kierra Smith (Canada), Jillian Tyler (Canada), Mike Brown (Canada), Keam Ang (Malaysia), and Yoav Meiri (Israel).
Academic excellence remains a cornerstone of Kremer’s programs. Both the men’s and women’s squads regularly earn CSCAA Scholar All-America Team honors, while routinely placing double-digit student-athletes on Academic All-Big Ten rosters each season. Among his notable academic standouts is Jessica Plant, a Rhodes Scholarship finalist who earned both the Big Ten Medal of Honor and the Big Ten Postgraduate Scholarship.
Before taking the helm at Minnesota, Kremer built a rich coaching foundation starting in 1988 with Springfield Aquatics. He later served as a graduate assistant at Drury University, head coach at John Brown University, and Assistant National Team Coach for the Mission Viejo Nadadores under legendary coach Bill Rose. As an athlete, Kremer was a 24-time NAIA National Champion and 29-time All-American at Drury University, placing fifth in the 100 backstroke at the 1991 U.S. Open and competing in the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials. He was inducted into the Drury Sports Hall of Fame in 1997.

Maddy Olson.b:
Maddy Olson enters her ninth season overall on the University of Minnesota swimming and diving staff in 2026–27, serving as Senior Associate Head Coach. Throughout her tenure, she has continually elevated the program through elite recruiting, student-athlete development, and poolside leadership.
Her coaching trajectory includes major milestones, highlighted by her selection to the U.S. World Teams coaching staff for the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore, where she guided top American swimmers including Gopher standout Joey Tepper on the U.S. Open Water Worlds Team. In May 2025, head coach Kelly Kremer announced her promotion to Associate Head Coach in recognition of her transformative contributions to team performance and recruitment strategy.
Olson originally joined the staff in May 2018 as an Assistant Coach and Coordinator of Recruiting and Communication, quickly establishing Minnesota as a national recruiting powerhouse. During her time in that role, she secured a top-16 national class for the women's team in 2019 and helped sign one of the highest-rated recruiting classes in program history in 2020.
Throughout her time working with the distance swim group, Olson has coached multiple Gophers to NCAA All-American performances, including: Bar Soloveychik, Megan Van Berkom, Eliot Kennedy, and Katie McCarthy.
A native of Champlin, Minnesota, Olson graduated from the University of Minnesota in 2016 with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism. Before transitioning into coaching, she spent three seasons covering Gopher swimming and diving as a journalist. She currently resides in Minneapolis with her dog, Frankie.

Zach Wood.b:
Zach Wood joined the Gopher Swim and Dive coaching staff in the fall of 2026 as an Assistant Coach.
"I'm immensely grateful to return to my alma mater and add another chapter to my University of Minnesota journey as a coach," said Wood. "This is an exciting chance for me to learn from an incredible coaching staff and make an impact on a group of amazing athletes that have chosen to be a part of our illustrious Gopher family legacy. I owe a debt of gratitude to Coach Kremer and the rest of the staff for being supportive and welcoming. Go Gophers!"
Wood most recently spent the 2025-26 season as the head coach of the swimming and diving program at Augsburg University. Wood helped lead the Auggies to a ninth place finish at the Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference (MIAC) Championships, guiding three of five athletes to personal best times.
Prior to his time at Augsburg, Wood served as a coach at the youth and collegiate levels. From 2012-13, Wood served as an Assistant Coach for the University of St. Thomas where he was part of second-place finishes for both the Tommies men's and women's programs in MIAC competition.
From 2008-13, Wood worked as a lead coach for the Minnetonka Swim Club where he helped grow the program from 115 swimmers to more than 330 and led athletes to numerous age-group state championship titles and several Minnesota High School state championship titles. Wood also served as head coach for the Black Dog Swimming Club in Burnsville, Minn., from 2013-14.
Wood competed for the University of Minnesota from 2003-07, earning multiple Big Ten finalist honors and qualifying for the NCAA Division I national championships twice while earning All-American honors in 2007. He was named the Gophers' most improved swimmer in his first season and was a team co-captain his senior year. Wood also competed on the USA Swimming national level from 2004-08, earning All-American honors with an eighth-place finish in the 200-yard butterfly in 2006. He also competed in three events at the 2008 US Olympic Trials.
Wood is a native of Alma, Mich., where he was inducted into the Alma School's Athletic Hall of Fame in 2016. He was a member of three Michigan state championship teams, was an eight-time individual state champion and an eight-time high school All-American. Wood was a three-time team MVP and team captain his senior year, setting school records in five different events and earning Michigan High School Swimmer of the Year honors in 2003.
"We are fortunate to welcome Zach as the newest member of our coaching staff!" said Director of Swimming and Diving, Kelly Kremer. "In addition to his love for Gopher Swimming and Diving, Zach brings new ideas, relentless energy, and a passion for swimming that is contagious!"

Zach Mertens.b:

Originally joining head coach Kelly Kremer’s staff as an assistant coach in August 2023, Mertens was promoted to Associate Head Coach ahead of the 2026–27 season. Since arriving in Minneapolis, he has been instrumental in developing the Gophers' sprint and middle-distance groups while playing a key role in team recruitment. Under his guidance, Minnesota student-athletes have earned multiple All-Big Ten selections, NCAA Championship qualifications, and academic honors.
Prior to joining the Golden Gophers, Mertens built an impressive coaching portfolio over six seasons (2017–2023) at Division II powerhouse Drury University, where he spent five years as a full-time assistant coach. During his time at Drury, he helped guide the Panthers to top-four national finishes for both the men's and women's programs, including NCAA DII men's national runner-up finishes. His work developing elite sprinters and relay squads earned him national recognition, culminating in his selection as one of six collegiate coaches nationwide to receive the prestigious Jean K. Freeman Scholarship in 2022.
A native of Saint Charles, Missouri, Mertens graduated in 2014 from Ouachita Baptist University, where he was a multi-year student-athlete for the Tigers swimming and diving program. Logan Redondo.b:
Redondo joined the Gopher coaching staff leading up to the 2026-27 season as an Assistant Coach for the swimming and diving program.
Redondo spent the 2025-26 season with the University of Virginia Swimming and Diving Program, serving as the Director of Professional Performance and Data Analysis. While with the Cavaliers, Redondo developed athlete performance profiling programs to help evaluate tactical performance, training adaptations, stroke efficiency, and race strategy in high-performance environments. Redondo also supported collegiate and professional swimmers while assisting coaching staff with recruiting evaluations and athlete performance projections.
“We are so excited to welcome Logan back to Minnesota as a Coach of the Gophers! Our student athletes will benefit from his experiences leading the Nadadores and working with UVA. Logan has done an outstanding job everywhere he’s been, and we are looking forward to the positive impact he will have on Minnesota Swimming and Diving!” said Director of Swimming and Diving, Kelly Kremer.
Before arriving at UVA, Redondo served as the head senior coach for the Mission Viejo Nadadores for four years. During Redondo’s time with the Nadadores, his swimmers earned 10 gold medals at Junior Nationals and won two individual high-point awards. His swimmers have set three national age group records, three Junior National meet records, more than 10 Southern California Swimming records and multiple Philippine and Venezuelan national records. He took the club from having no athletes above the US Open level to having seven US Nationals qualifiers, four US Junior National team members, three Olympic Trials qualifiers and one senior national team member on the United States, Philippines and Venezuelan squads.
“I am so grateful for the opportunity to return to the University of Minnesota and continue building upon its historic legacy, now as a coach. I want to thank the staff at the University of Virginia and Cavalier Aquatics, as I would not have this opportunity without their support, as well as Coach Kelly Kremer and the Gopher staff for believing in me and giving me this opportunity. Redondo swam four years at the University of Minnesota, representing the Gophers at the Big Ten and NCAA championships. He graduated from the University of Minnesota in 2017 with a BS in Kinesiology with an emphasis in Sport Psychology.

Zachary Hawley.b:
Hawley enters his second season with the Gophers in 2026-27 after joining Minnesota from New Mexico State, where he helped lead all aspects of their diving program, including recruiting, training, culture development, and meet operations. During his time with the Aggies, he played a major role in developing the program's first ever NCAA Zone Diving finalist.
"Zach is a very accomplished diving coach, and we are fortunate to have him join our program this fall! It will be a lot of fun watching Wenbo and Zach team up to help our divers reach their full potential!" said Director of Swimming and Diving, Kelly Kremer.
Before New Mexico State, Hawley spent nine seasons as the Head Diving Coach at George Mason University where he was a three-time Atlantic-10 Diving Coach of the Year. At George Mason, he also played a part in developing four conference champions and an NCAA qualifier. He also coached three A-10 Diver of the Year award recipients and led 13 individuals to Division I NCAA Zone Qualifiers.
Hawley made quite a name for himself while in Fairfax, Virginia, as he also was the owner and head coach of the Mason Dive Academy which provides a dive program for athletes of all ages and skill levels. Coach Hawley made it his mission to build and develop strong, successful and confident young individuals in the sport of diving with the ultimate goal of getting these values to carry over to other facets of life.
Prior to his tenure at George Mason, Hawley spent two years with South Dakota State University as a graduate assistant where he played a vital role in SDSU's transition into a Division I program.
While at South Dakota State, his athletes broke all the program's diving records and Hawley helped guide the Jackrabbits to their first NCAA Zone Qualifiers in school history.
From 2010-2012, Hawley traveled across the nation during the summer to spend time with some of the top coaches in the nation. These trips included spending time working at several collegiate camps including camps at The University of Texas at Austin, The University of Indiana and The University of Missouri.
"I'm incredibly excited to be joining the Golden Gopher staff as the Assistant Diving Coach. This is a fantastic opportunity for me to continue learning and growing as a coach, with the added bonus of returning to the Midwest. The University of Minnesota holds a special place in my journey; it's where I attended my first-ever diving camps and where I've competed many times as both an athlete and a coach.
I've been fortunate to have success at the national age group level and within NCAA Division I mid-major programs. I'm eager to learn from a highly respected coaching staff that has produced Big Ten champions, NCAA champions, and Olympic medalists," said Hawley.
Hawley earned a bachelor's in Physical Education, Exercise Science, and Wellness from the University of North Dakota in 2009. He also pursued master's degree work in Kinesiology at UND, as well as Sports Pedagogy and Recreational Management at South Dakota State University.

Wenbo Chen.b:
Wenbo Chen enters his 18th season as the Head Men's and Women's Diving Coach at the University of Minnesota for the 2026–27 academic year. Throughout his tenure in Minneapolis, Chen has established the Gophers as one of the premier collegiate diving programs in the nation. Under his guidance, Minnesota divers have claimed four NCAA National Championships, over 70 CSCAA All-America honors, and more than 20 Big Ten individual conference titles.
Chen's impact on Minnesota's national profile began early in his tenure when he coached Kelci Bryant to back-to-back NCAA individual titles (3-meter in 2010, 1-meter in 2011). That legacy continued with Yu Zhou, who won the 3-meter NCAA title in both 2015 and 2017 while earning CSCAA Diver of the Year honors in 2015. Under Chen’s tutelage, Sarah Bacon went on to become the most decorated female athlete in University of Minnesota history, winning five NCAA National Championships—capturing 1-meter titles in 2018, 2019, and 2021, along with 3-meter titles in 2021 and 2022—and finishing her career as a 10-time All-American.
The program's championship standard has continued through recent seasons. In 2023–24, Chen coached sophomore Vivi Del Angel to Minnesota's first-ever national championship in women's platform diving. That same season, freshman Elna Widerstrom earned All-American status on the 1-meter board, while freshman YuTong Wang secured dual All-America honors across both springboards and became Minnesota's first men's Big Ten diving champion since 2016. In 2025–26, Chen earned his 11th Big Ten Diving Coach of the Year award as Widerstrom was named Big Ten Diver of the Year following her conference title on the 1-meter board and a bronze medal finish at the NCAA Championships. Meanwhile, Del Angel wrapped up her collegiate career as an 8-time All-American after taking the 2026 Big Ten platform diving crown.
Beyond collegiate competition, Chen possesses extensive international and Olympic credentials. He served as an assistant coach for the U.S. Olympic Diving Team at three Olympic Games: London 2012, Rio 2016, and Paris 2024. At the 2012 Games, he guided Gopher standout Kelci Bryant and teammate Abby Johnston to a silver medal in synchronized 3-meter diving. Before moving to the United States in 1992, Chen headed the Chinese National Team from 1983 to 1991, coaching six Olympic medalists, including two-time Olympic gold medalists Ni Xiong and Ming Gao.
As an athlete, Chen won a Chinese junior national title on the 3-meter springboard in 1976 and was a senior national finalist from 1977 to 1982. He earned his bachelor's degree in physical education from Beijing Sports University in 1987. Chen lives in the Twin Cities with his wife, Wenyin Han, and they have two daughters, Amy and Annie.

Michael Hampel.b:
Hampel enters his second season with the Gophers in 2026-27 after joining Minnesota from Southern Illinois University, where he spent the 2024-25 season as the Assistant Swimming Coach. During his time with the Salukis, Hampel oversaw the workouts of the Breastroke and IM groups while assisting with sprint group practices and playing a role in the recruitment of domestic and international athletes for the program. With his help, the Salukis finished as the highest scoring Division I mid-major in last season's Women's NCAA Championships while setting 27 Missouri Valley Conference records and 38 program records in the process.
"Michael comes highly recommended from numerous coaches and administrators within our profession. He is early in this profession, but his passion for teaching, coaching, and recruiting student-athletes is clear the second you meet him! Michael is an outstanding fit for our program and we are looking forward to his arrival in Minneapolis!" said Director of Swimming and Diving, Kelly Kremer.
Prior to SIU, Hampel was the leader of the sprint group at Keiser University, helping the women claim their third straight NAIA National Championship and leading their men to a runner-up finish at the NAIA National Championship. The women wrapped up the three-peat with 44 NAIA All-Americans, five relay All-American teams, four relay national championship teams, and three individual national championships. The men grabbed 45 NAIA All-Americans, five relay All-American teams, two relay national championship teams, and four individual national championships.
Before Keiser, he helped lead the University of West Florida swimming & diving program to their fourth consecutive NSISC Conference Championship and sixth overall in the program's tenth year. During his time in Pensacola, Hampel also helped lead the Argos to the largest margin of victory in NSISC history (407 points), the largest NCAA roster for the Argos in school history (16), 28 NCAA All-Americans, 45 Argos Top 10 All-Time Performances, and five school records.
"I am extremely excited to be joining the University of Minnesota Swimming and Diving staff. The leadership and loyalty to Minnesota this staff has shown is something difficult to find in today's college landscape. I am humbled to be a part of this community, University, and truly elite program. I cannot wait to help these student-athletes reach their God-given potential in and out of the pool. Go Gophers!"
Hampel earned a bachelor's in General Studies with an emphasis in Biomedical Science, Kinesiology, and Psychology from Missouri State University in 2022. He also earned a master's in professional studies with an emphasis and graduate certificate in Sports Management.
